articles.title: Library book ‘scam’: Madras High Court had sounded warning two years ago, called for enquiry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Against the backdrop of writer Perumal Murugan’s expose on substandard books containing grossly erroneous historical information making their way into the shelves of the Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore, it would be worthwhile to take a look at how the court had sought to streamline procurement of books

“This is nothing short of a scam,” wrote the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on the alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for public libraries in Tamil Nadu, while calling upon the government to constitute a committee to enquire into the allegations made by a petitioner in June 2024. A Bench of Justices R. Mahadevan and G.R. Swaminathan also gave directions on transparent procedures to be followed in the procurement of books.

Against the backdrop of writer Perumal Murugan’s expose on substandard books containing grossly erroneous historical information making their way into the shelves of the Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore, it would be worthwhile to take a look at how the court had sought to streamline procurement of books.
S. Krishnan, who runs a literary forum in Nagercoil, had moved the court in 2019 (when the AIADMK was in power) alleging irregularities in the purchase of books for public libraries.

“He [petitioner] brings to our notice the scandalous state of affairs prevalent in the procurement of books for public libraries in Tamil Nadu,” the court noted. “The petitioner describes the modus operandi in detail in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition. His statements are not made in the air. He provides solid proof and justification,” the Judges said.

As per norms, once a book is purchased for a public library, it cannot be purchased again for the next five years. “It is seen that this condition has been flagrantly breached. Nationalised books are re-printed and published under different titles and authors’ names and procured every year. This is nothing short of a scam,” the court said.

Mr Krishnan, in his petition, enclosed a report published in The Hindu dated January 11, 2019, in which one publisher had alleged that 99% of the books printed exclusively for the Government Library orders would not be available in the open market. Another publisher lamented that a publisher runs a dozen publications in different names only for the sake of getting Government orders and that quality has suffered setback. It was also alleged that 95% of the books were actually by publishers who are ready to pay commission to officials dealing with library orders.

Strangely, for five years the government did not file its counter-affidavit, prompting the court to record, “the rule of non- traverse will apply and we have to take it that the allegations made by the petitioner stand unrebutted.” Thereafter the Government Pleader submitted the School Education Department’s Government Order (G.O.) dated March 7, 2024, laying down the Transparent Book Procurement Policy 2024. This G.O. acknowledged unfair practices such as sale of books by changing the title or the author’s name.

However, the Judges said: “The case of the petitioner is that the procurement done so far has facilitated such unfair practices. Bathing in Ganga is believed to wash away one’s past sins. But the issuance of G.O cannot absolve the department of the misdeeds committed in the past by the officials.”

Allowing the writ petition, the Judges issued directions on procurement of books. They said the Director Public Libraries must maintain a dedicated, user friendly and functional website and spread awareness about it through social media.

Going a step further, it directed the Government to constitute a committee to enquire into the allegations made by the petitioner. “Views will be elicited from the various publishers in this regard. A comprehensive report shall be published within five months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. It should catalogue all the unfair practices that have come to light so far. Action should be taken against the officials concerned. An action taken report should also be published in the Website within six months thereafter. If necessary, the persons concerned should be prosecuted,” the court said.

articles.title: Delhi High Court grants 7-day custody parole to Al Falah University chairman to tend to ailing wife
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi High Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) granted seven-day custody parole to Al Falah University group chairman Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui, who is in custody in two money laundering cases, to take care of his ailing wife.
The court passed the order after hearing Siddiqui’s plea seeking interim bail or custody parole for a week on medical and humanitarian grounds.
Mr Siddiqui said his wife is a Stage-4 ovarian cancer patient and has to undergo the next cycle of chemotherapy on November 10.

The Enforcement Directorate (ED) opposed Siddiqui’s interim release as the allegations against him were serious. The ED’s counsel submitted that the accused was a flight risk and had criminal antecedents, including his involvement in the November 2025 Red Fort car blast case.

articles.title: Delhi air 'very poor' with AQI reading of 364
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital
The national capital woke up to yet another day of very poor air on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning, a day before Diwali, which forecasts suggest is likely to impact the air quality further.

The air quality index (AQI) at 9 a.m. on Saturday (November 7) stood at 364 (very poor), as compared to the 24-hour average AQI of 382 at 4 p.m. on Friday (November 6), according to data from the Central Board of Pollution Control (CPCB).
As per CPCB standards, an AQI of 0-50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor', and 401-500 'severe'.
Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, 18 recorded AQI in the severe category on Saturday (November 7) morning.

According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to reach the severe category on Saturday (November 7). Several weather stations saw a slight dip in the minimum temperature.

Safdarjung, representative of the city's weather, recorded a minimum of 16.2 degrees Celsius, 1.9°C below the normal and one degree less than Friday (November 6). According to IMD forecast, mostly clear skies are expected for the next few days.
The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital.

The directive, issued Friday (November 7), applies to all government, government-aided and unaided recognised private schools under the Directorate of Education, as well as those run by the NDMC, MCD and Delhi Cantonment Board.
All the government and private schools in Delhi will conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode, allowing students to attend either in person or online, it stated.

According to the circular, the decision was taken in compliance with the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) order invoking all actions under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across Delhi-NCR.

articles.title: Keralam Child Development Centre gets ₹35-lakh grant to study autism-related parental grief
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Three-year project will examine chronic sorrow and coping mechanisms in ASD families.

The Child Development Centre (CDC), Thiruvananthapuram, has received an Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)-approved grant of ₹35 lakh for a three-year research project titled “Development and Validation of a Tool for Assessing Grief among Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.”
The project, led by CDC director Deepa Bhaskaran, aims to develop and validate a culturally relevant tool to assess grief among parents of children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).

“The study will use focus group discussions and in-depth interviews involving parents of children with ASD, bereaved parents, professionals working with children with ASD, and members of the general population to understand the dimensions and cultural expressions of grief in the Indian context,” Dr. Bhaskaran said.

According to her, parents commonly experience shock, denial, fear, guilt, anger, sadness, and helplessness following their child’s diagnosis. The grief, described as chronic sorrow or non-finite grief, can recur at different stages of the child’s development, particularly when expected developmental milestones are not attained.

“The findings will help facilitate the identification of grief-related concerns among parents and support the development of appropriate grief counselling protocols and support group interventions, ultimately contributing to improved psychosocial well-being among families of children with ASD,” she said.
Inadequate social support compounds parental distress, she noted.

“There is a need for healthcare professionals to recognise and assess parents’ emotional well-being alongside the rehabilitation needs of children with autism. Early diagnosis, psychological support, and training for professionals to identify grief and help families develop coping strategies are vital,” she added.

articles.title: Secret Service arrests man near White House after he said he heard voices telling him to kill Trump
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill the Republican President

The U.S. Secret Service said a suspect has been taken into custody and charged after officers found him in a vehicle near the White House with multiple guns, claiming he heard voices in his head telling him to kill President Donald Trump .
The arrest Thursday night (November 7, 2026) happened after Secret Service officers approached a man "acting suspicious" in a parked car, according to a Homeland Security statement.
U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation's capital and kill the Republican President.
Shortly after, officers discovered the suspect's vehicle had been reported stolen and he had three different firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition.

This is the latest in a series of arrests the Secret Service and other law enforcement agencies have made against individuals who have threatened Trump or his family members' lives since he returned to office last year.

The statement described Chrinos as a migrant from Venezuela who is in the country illegally after entering the U.S. through Texas in March 2024. DHS said he has been charged and currently remains in U.S. Marshals Service custody.
The White House did not provide comment, instead referring to DHS and USSS.

"Thanks to our brave Secret Service officers, this illegal alien with three firearms in his vehicle was arrested near the White House before he could harm anyone," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in the statement.

articles.title: Jay Rockefeller, heir to famed dynasty and healthcare advocate in U.S. Senate, dies at 89
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jay Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.
His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”
He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”

He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.

New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

articles.title: U.S. military carries out fresh targeted strikes on Iran as Tehran weighs mediator's proposals
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,’ says U.S. President Trump
President Donald Trump said the U.S. military on Friday (November 6, 2026) carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defence system.
Iran state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the crucial waterway for oil shipments.
Mr. Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as "minor".

"They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Mr. Trump told reporters shortly after arriving in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday (November 6) evening.

Mr. Trump did not offer further details about the target. U.S. officials have reported that most of Iran's air defence systems were destroyed or severely degraded during a June 2025 bombardment by Israel and in the early stages of the current conflict. U.S. officials have assessed that Iran would try to rebuild them and other military infrastructure over time.

The U.S. military also reported carrying out what it described as defensive strikes on Monday (November 2). Explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
Friday's (November 7) strikes are the first since Mr. Trump's Republican Party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday's (November 3) midterm elections in the U.S.

The electoral setback was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Mr. Trump's execution of the conflict and elevated fuel prices, a byproduct of the war that's affected nearly every sector of the global economy.
In the days since Republicans' shellacking at the polls, Mr. Trump has vacillated between threatening to "destroy" Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.

Earlier on Friday (November 6), officials from the two West Asian governments said Iran is reviewing proposals presented by chief mediator Qatar aimed at addressing differences with the U.S. about Tehran's nuclear programme.

articles.title: China says discussions underway on Xi-Trump-Putin meeting
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: President Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen to meet President Xi for the third time this year, as the fragile trade truce is set to expire in January
Beijing has confirmed for the first time that it is discussing a historic meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Mao Ning, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry, said at a press briefing this week in Beijing that China "is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state."
Nothing is set, but the three-leader gathering would take place this month on the sidelines of a regional summit in Shenzhen.

If it happens, it would be historic. Experts, however, say the three leaders are unlikely to discuss anything substantive because their interests are at odds, but they would gather for a photo, with China carefully choreographing the meeting.
"I think it will happen. The question is the format and the content," said Sun Yun, director of the China programme at the Stimson Center. "China wants the image but not the costs."
Beijing is the host of this year's leaders’ summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, a 21-member grouping that includes the U.S. and Russia.
President Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen to meet President Xi for the third time this year, as the fragile trade truce is set to expire in January.

In a sign that tensions persist, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, in a Friday (November 6, 2026) video call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, urged Beijing to take "concrete actions to fully implement its past commitments, particularly as they relate to agricultural purchases, rare earths, and other critical minerals," according to a statement from Greer's office.

China's official news agency Xinhua reported Saturday (November 7) that both sides held in-depth, constructive exchanges on the call, and that China expressed concerns about Washington's restrictive economic and trade measures against Beijing.

While he's in China, Mr. Trump has said he would be interested in meeting Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin to discuss nuclear arms control, though Mr. Putin is focused on talking about the war in Ukraine without Kyiv at the table.

Both officials were not authorised to comment publicly on the delicate negotiations and spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Iran and Qatari officials’ stepped-up engagement — and Tehran showing a glint of openness to the possibility of negotiating on its nuclear programme — comes just days after Trump’s Republican Party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the U.S.

articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

A few kilometres from the entrance to Arunachal Pradesh’s Parong village, an unpaved road winds all the way down to the Siang river. At dusk, all that is visible at the beginning of the dirt road is the glint of freshly painted yellow barricades of the State police and the shine from the silver of the concertina wires that connect the barricades. The Central security forces who guard the check post here have two purposes — to respond to “unrest” and to stop anyone without “clearance” from proceeding to Siang’s waters.

Parong, in Siang district, is one of the three proposed sites identified by the State government for a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to begin work on the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

articles.title: OpenAI to press ahead with data-centre expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO says
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth

OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-centre expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fuelled fears of tighter scrutiny ​of the facilities, its Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar told CNBC in an interview on Friday.

“When ‌I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how ​do we keep investing to meet customer demand,” Friar said. “We are ⁠going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can get the compute we need,” she added.

One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth. It launched a charm offensive on Thursday to win ‌over communities as opposition to data centres becomes a rallying point for anxieties ‌about ⁠the technology.

As part of the efforts, OpenAI said, it will no ⁠longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites. It will also give residents access to construction plans and their potential effects.

Growing data-centre opposition was a crucial issue in the midterm ​elections. Democratic candidates, including Texas Governor-elect Gina ‌Hinojosa, made tighter scrutiny of the facilities a central campaign pledge. The Lone Star State is one of the fastest-growing data-center regions in the world.

Fears the Democratic sweep may slow construction of the facilities critical to the AI boom ‌wiped about $2.5 trillion off the US stock market on Thursday, as investors ​weighed the fallout for the chip, cloud and networking industries that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the spending frenzy.
Still, there are ⁠signs that tech giants remain committed to data-centre expansion plans despite the growing backlash.
Alphabet-owned Google said on Thursday it would invest $17 billion to build its first data centre ‌in Wyoming.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance is considering expanding a data centre project in northeastern Brazil, a move that would strengthen its standing as Latin America’s leading builder of computing facilities.
Friar also told CNBC that OpenAI was raising fresh capital, pushing back against suggestions the ChatGPT maker had scaled back its fundraising ambitions amid the sharp AI stocks selloff.

articles.title: Activists invade site of Microsoft's planned data centre in Amsterdam
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: "It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Geef Tegengas spokesman, Nathan Timmer, told AFP
Several hundred activists opposed to the construction of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam occupied the site on Friday, responding to a call for a two-day protest across Europe.
The collective Geef Tegengas, which campaigns for climate and justice, and the environmental group Fossielvrij entered the construction site in the Sloterdijk district, halting work for the day.
"It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Geef Tegengas spokesman, Nathan Timmer, told AFP.
"This thing will use as much energy as all of the households in Amsterdam combined... this thing will use a ridiculous amount of water."
Timmer, 30, also argued that the centre would be used "to facilitate AI warfare" and what he called the "genocide" in Gaza.
The activists made it on to the site by scaling barrier fences despite a police presence.
Once inside they shouted political slogans and sprayed anti-Microsoft messages on walls under construction.
Dutch news agency ANP reported that police arrested between 150 and 200 protesters. Other activists quit the site voluntarily.
AI data centres require large amounts of electricity, placing increased pressure on grids often still reliant on fossil fuels, and, in many cases, water to cool down hot computing equipment.
A backlash is growing worldwide against their environmental impact, and there are also concerns over noise, pollution, their appearance and how many jobs the facilities actually create.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt sanctions ₹198 crore as honorarium for officials involved in 2026 Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Government order, issued by the Public (Elections) Department, stated one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officials and staff members involved in 2026 Assembly election

The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.
Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

A Government order, issued by the Public (Elections) Department, stated one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officials and staff members involved in 2026 Assembly election

The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.

Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

articles.title: OMCs refute Karnataka’s E20 report, seeks additional details about procedure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The state-owned OMCs held the 56 samples tested by them from across the state reported an average 19.3% ethanol content in the vehicular fuel.

Refuting observations about ethanol blend in petrol being as high as 31% in Karnataka, the three state-owned oil-marketing companies (OMCs) stated the tests were not conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedure.

Citing discrepancies with findings from their own quality monitoring, they urged the State government to share the complete counterpart sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports, and details about the adopted testing methodology, and samples for retesting.

“The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the state government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2024,” it stated, adding, “Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with applicable guidelines.”
The OMCs raised concerns about the Karnataka Dept of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology’s use of the gas chromatography for evaluating ethanol concentration.
The process broadly entails separating compounds via vaporisation.

According to the OMCs, the certificates cited for the State government’s observations do not specify the applicable standard test method, the procedure for diluting the compounds or the reference material used for correction after vaporisation.
“In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26-31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021,” the statement read.

Further, pointing to the Karnataka government’s reported observations, it observed, “Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy [in Karnataka’s reported samples] further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.”
The three OMCs put forth that 56 samples from across the State tested by them conformed to the prescribed specifications, reporting ethanol content between at an average 19.3%.
Thus, arguing that the “substantially higher ethanol levels” reported by the State Dept. warrant a “transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.”

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results LIVE: Counting under way across 365 centres amidst high security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and other top officials are monitoring the counting.
Both TDP and YSRCP are hopeful of victory in Kotia group of villages of Salur mandal of Parvatipuram Manyam district where poll percentage is around 35%.
This, in spite of strong objection from Odisha over conduct of local body elections in those villages located at the AP-Odisha border.

The counting of votes for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections began peacefully across Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district on Saturday, with the district administration making elaborate arrangements to ensure a smooth and transparent process.

Counting is being taken up simultaneously across all 11 mandals in the district including headquarters at Paderu. A total of 298 counting tables have been arranged, with 149 tables each for MPTC and ZPTC constituencies to facilitate the counting process.
Approximately 1,200 counting personnel have been deployed for the exercise.

As many as 103 candidates, who contested for 27 ZPTC seats, are eagerly waiting for results in Vizianagaram district. TDP which won 11 MPTC segments unanimously is hopeful of winning in majority seats out of 438 MPTC segments. As many as 1,066 candidates tested their luck in those seats.
As counting of the votes is under way for ZPTC and MPTC polls, TDP is seen gaining a lead in postal ballots in Vizianagaram, Bondapalli, Dattirajeru, Gajapathinagaram and other mandals.

The counting of votes for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) rural local body elections commenced peacefully across NTR district on Saturday morning.
The counting centres have been set up at nine places across the district for 16 ZPTC and 276 MPTC seats, with all necessary basic facilities provided.

For smooth conduct of the counting process, 18 counting halls and 281 counting tables have been arranged. Around 1,500 counting supervisors, counting assistants and other supporting staff have been deployed.

articles.title: Delhi air ‘very poor’ with AQI reading of 364
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital
The national capital woke up to yet another day of very poor air on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning, a day before Diwali, which forecasts suggest is likely to impact the air quality further.

The air quality index (AQI) at 9 a.m. on Saturday (November 7) stood at 364 (very poor), as compared to the 24-hour average AQI of 382 at 4 p.m. on Friday (November 6), according to data from the Central Board of Pollution Control (CPCB).
As per CPCB standards, an AQI of 0-50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor', and 401-500 'severe'.
Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, 18 recorded AQI in the severe category on Saturday (November 7) morning.

According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to reach the severe category on Saturday (November 7). Several weather stations saw a slight dip in the minimum temperature.

Safdarjung, representative of the city's weather, recorded a minimum of 16.2 degrees Celsius, 1.9°C below the normal and one degree less than Friday (November 6). According to IMD forecast, mostly clear skies are expected for the next few days.
The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital.

The directive, issued Friday (November 7), applies to all government, government-aided and unaided recognised private schools under the Directorate of Education, as well as those run by the NDMC, MCD and Delhi Cantonment Board.
All the government and private schools in Delhi will conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode, allowing students to attend either in person or online, it stated.

According to the circular, the decision was taken in compliance with the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) order invoking all actions under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across Delhi-NCR.

articles.title: Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Republic’s armed forces, having gained experience from direct confrontation with United States and Israel, are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war, Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

articles.title: NSUI sends knives, cutters to BJP leader Chalavadi Narayanaswamy’s residence over controversial remarks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka unit of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) on Saturday sent knives and cutters to the residence of BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, through online delivery platforms, in protest against his alleged remarks targeting Congress leaders.
Several delivery executives reportedly arrived at Mr. Narayanaswamy’s residence with packages containing knives and cutters, despite the BJP leader not having placed any such orders.
NSUI State president Kirthi Ganesh subsequently released a video statement confirming that the student organisation had deliberately placed the orders as a form of protest.
The protest was reportedly triggered by remarks allegedly made by Mr. Narayanaswamy that Congress leaders should be “cut into pieces and thrown into the Arabian Sea”.

He also appealed to Congress and NSUI workers across the State to place similar online orders to the BJP leader's residence. Mr. Ganesh claimed that he had circulated Mr. Narayanaswamy’s residential address and phone number online to facilitate the campaign.
Concluding his statement, Mr. Ganesh challenged the BJP leader not to harm even a single Congress worker, warning him against acting on the alleged threat.

articles.title: Assam OIL facility fire death toll rises to three
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two workers succumbed to their injuries at a private hospital in Guwahati on November 7
Two of the six persons injured in Friday’s (November 6, 2026) fire following an explosion at an Oil India Limited (OIL) facility in eastern Assam’s Dibrugarh died on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Tapas Gogoi, working for a Mumbai-based private agency engaged by the oil exploration major, succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital in Dibrugarh town at around 3 a.m.

Another worker, Rupam Gogoi, died at a private hospital in Guwahati at around 11 a.m., taking the death toll in the fire incident to three. He was shifted from the Assam Medical College and Hospital in Dibrugarh for advanced treatment.
The third person, identified as Raju Dutta, died from the impact of the explosion on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The fire broke out around 9.05 a.m. at the indirect bath heater in OIL’s intermediate tank farm at Tengakhat. The bath heater was isolated on November 4 for maintenance.
Four other workers injured in the incident are undergoing treatment.
According to OIL, fire and emergency services personnel rushed to the facility and launched fire-fighting operations to extinguish the fire by 12.30 p.m. on Friday (November 6, 2026).

OIL constituted an internal inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify its immediate and underlying causes, assess damage and suggest proactive measures to prevent such incidents in future, officials said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

articles.title: Enforcement Directorate is not a ‘super cop’, says Karnataka High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ED cannot file private complaint when other agencies decline to act on its information on alleged offences, court said while quashing ED cases against K.Y. Nanjegowda, Congress MLA from Malur

In a setback to the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) , the High Court of Karnataka has held that the ED is “not a super cop” and cannot file a private complaint to initiate a money-laundering probe when the competent agencies decline to prosecute a scheduled offence based on the information filed by the ED.

The Court ruled that the ED’s power under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act (PMLA) is “derivative and not original”, and that filing a private complaint under Section 200 Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) / Section 223 Bharatiya Nagarik Surakasha Sanhita is not contemplated under the PMLA Act.

“... one institution in the country does not become supreme so that it is in a position to abuse the powers conferred on it. Law recognises the requirements of checks and balances. The ED is not a super cop to investigate anything and everything which comes into its notice,” the Court observed, adding that the ED must exercise only those powers expressly conferred on it by the PMLA.

Justice M.I. Arun passed the order while allowing a batch of writ petitions filed by Congress Party MLA from Malur constituency K.Y. Nanjegowda, who is also Chairman of the Kolar and Chikkaballapur Milk Union Ltd. (KOMUL), Y.B. Ashwathanarayana then Director of KOMUL, K.N. Gopala Murthy, Nagesh N. and Raju Krishna C.

The petitioners had challenged the ED’s ECIR registered in November 2023, the Adjudicating Authority’s order confirming seizure of articles, summons issued to them, and the private complaint filed by the ED before a special court.

The case stemmed from the criminal proceedings initiated based on a private complaint on “land scam” lodged by one K.C. Rajanna before a trial court in Kolar alleging irregularities in the grant of about 80 acres of land to 38 persons by the Malur Land Grant Committee, of which Mr. Nanjegowda was chairman.

Treating this case it as a predicate offence, the ED had registered ECIR in 2023. During searches conducted based in this ECIR, the ED agency claimed to have stumbled upon material indicating irregularities in recruitments to the KOMUL, which it termed a separate “job scam.” Further, the ED had shared with the Karnataka Lokayukta police the information on alleged “job scam” that it had discovered during the searches.

However, the “land scam” case ended in a closure report by the jurisdictional police, and the trial court dismissed it for want of sanction to prosecute a public servant even though complainant Mr. Rajanna protested against closure report.

As the Lokayukta police did not act on the information shared by it under Section 66(2) of the PMLA), the ED itself had filed a private complaint before a special court in Bengaluru on KOMUL “job scam.”

It was argued in behalf of the petitioners that once the predicate offence collapses, even on technical grounds, the ED cannot continue PMLA proceedings, and that when ED uncovers a different scheduled offence, its only permissible course is to share information with the competent agency and not filling a separate private complaint and probe it.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh government hikes DA by 3% for employees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63%, up from 60%. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the State government said in a statement on November 7

The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 3% for State government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales.

Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63%, up from 60%. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the State government said in a statement on Saturday (November 7, 2026). A Government Order was also issued in this regard on Saturday.
The enhanced Dearness Allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the State.

“The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the State's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees,” the statement said.

articles.title: Vance distancing himself from Trump ahead of 2028 Presidential race: Ex-U.S. NSA Bolton
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bolton described Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Trump's tariff policies

U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance is trying to distance himself from President Donald Trump by blaming the Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war as he prepares for a potential 2028 Presidential bid, former U.S. national security adviser John Bolton has said.

In an interview with PTI Videos , Mr. Bolton described Mr. Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Mr. Trump's tariff policies.

"There's no doubt that part of the underlying reason for Mr. Vance’s statement was that this is the beginning of his 2028 nomination campaign. And he's trying something very politically risky here," he said.
Mr. Bolton argued that the Iran war was only one factor behind voter discontent, pointing out that Mr. Trump's tariffs had contributed to persistently high prices.
He said Mr. Trump had promised during the 2024 Presidential campaign to address economic concerns better than the Biden administration, but had failed to deliver after taking office.

"The voters took him at his word. They said we have more faith that Mr. Trump can handle these issues than Mr. Biden and Ms. Harris. So he gets elected, he comes in, and he doesn't do it. And if anything, he's causing more problems," the former U.S. NSA said.

Mr. Bolton also emphasised how the Iran war pushed up international oil and gas prices and increased energy costs for American consumers. "What they opposed was the higher price of gasoline. And Mr. Trump didn't even attempt to address that," he added.

He described the Democrats' strong midterm performance as a "stinging repudiation" of Mr. Trump, saying voters across party lines were tired of his leadership, though the results did not necessarily amount to an endorsement of the blue team.
He also said Mr. Trump was unlikely to fundamentally change his leadership style during the remaining two years of his term, despite the electoral setback.
"Trump's whole operating style for 10 years is: I don't work with anybody. I represent the people, and I'm going to do what I want to do," Mr. Bolton stated.

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week . In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.

Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.

Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. ⁠As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.

He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served ‌as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies ‌such as Nike of discriminating against white people.
His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former ⁠communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.
As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.

Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, ‌not just those with criminal records.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

fullParagraphs: New Zealand’s election remained too close to call on November 7, as early results trickled in from across the country, with neither the governing National-Luxon coalition nor Labour falling short of a majority and minor parties weighing in, including a rising Opportunity Party

The outcome of New Zealand's election remained too close to call as early results began to roll in on Saturday (November 7, 2026), with none of the parties expected to secure a majority after a campaign dominated by worries over rising costs of living and the economy.
Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet — the price of basic goods remains stubbornly high, and unemployment is at its highest in more than a decade.
The war in West Asia and the subsequent global fuel shock have been widely blamed for the hit to New Zealand's trade-dependent economy.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon hoped his right-wing coalition could cling to power with promises of no new taxes, after three fractious years in office, two failed bids by his own National Party to oust him as leader and an economy in the doldrums.
Former Premier Chris Hipkins' centre-left Labour have promised help with living costs, from free doctor's visits and prescriptions to a cap on public transport fares.
He said on Friday (November 6) he was sure his party would "exceed expectations".
At a Labour event in Upper Hutt near Wellington bedecked with red balloons, party workers were quietly confident they had secured the largest number of seats.
And at a National gathering in the country's largest city of Auckland, cheers rose from the crowd as the party's candidates were shown to be ahead.
Police minister and National lawmaker Mark Mitchell told journalists it was "very close".
"When you reflect on what's happening globally, we certainly see lots of geopolitical uncertainty," he said.

articles.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, first Muslim U.S. Senator-elect?

fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), according to media projections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber and preserving a crucial Democratic seat in the party’s fight for Senate control.

His victory denied Republicans the chance to fill the seat left vacant by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. The 42-year-old former public health official ran on a progressive platform focused ⁠on lowering costs for working families and ⁠reducing corporate influence in politics.
His win marked a breakthrough for the Democratic Party’s progressive wing ‌in this closely contested midterm election cycle.

Abdul El-Sayed was born on October 31 , 1984, in Rochester Hills, Michigan, U.S.. He attended public schools, where he captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams. He was raised by his father, Mohamed, an Egyptian immigrant and his stepmom, Jackie, whose family has lived in Gratiot County, Michigan since the 1800s. Mr. El-Sayed earned his undergraduate degree with the highest distinction from the University of Michigan where he also played on the Wolverine men’s lacrosse team. He went on to earn a medical degree from Columbia University under an NIH-funded fellowship, as well as a second doctorate from Oxford University as Rhodes Scholer.
He lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku and their two daughters.

Although trained as a physician, Mr. El-Sayed shifted his focus to public service after realising the political systemic issues that was deteriorating public health, according to his campaign website.

He rebuilt Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy and led Wayne County’s Department of Health. Human & Veterans Services, serving 1.8 million residents. His public service spans several achievements, including securing free eyeglasses for children, targeting major environmental polluters, making the life-saving Narcan universally accessible and pioneering a programme projected to cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 3,00,000 Michiganders, as per the website.

He authored Medicare for All: A Citizen’s Guide and served on former President Biden’s 2020 Unity Task Force for Healthcare to help develop policies aimed at lowering prescription drug costs. His public service earned him recognition as “Public Official of the Year” by the Michigan LCV and also a spot on Crain’s Detroit Business 40 Under 40 list.

Mr. El-Sayed won the U.S. Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. He launched his campaign to lower living costs and ensure government agencies serve working people rather than billionaires.

Mr. Rogers, 63, ‌a former Congressman and FBI agent, entered ​the race with strong backing from President Trump and national Republicans and sought ⁠to cast Mr. El-Sayed as a radical candidate sympathetic to Islamic extremism through alleged ties to the Muslim ‌Brotherhood, claims that Mr. El-Sayed denies and that remain unsupported by evidence. Democrats said the attacks on Mr. El-Sayed relied on Islamophobic tropes, according to Reuters.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Doctors warn that there is no replacement for natural solutions, and supplements cannot be taken over a long period

If a good night’s sleep has become your holy grail, who are the knights in shining armour you will employ to reach that chalice? Most people seem to be deploying melatonin and magnesium supplements, over the counter, but the question that remains is: are they effective, and if so, at what combinations or levels?

The consensus among most sleep specialists, is that both melatonin and magnesium (glycinate) can have an ameliorative impact – in the short term. Both these supplements, however, work differently – while melatonin is a key body clock signal, magnesium helps relax the body. When and how you take both supplements makes a great deal of difference to your hours of sleep and sleep quality as well.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

fullParagraphs: The U.S. regulators warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems,” shortly after these hacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarkets
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and government regulators on Thursday (November 5, 2026) issued a warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial coolers and fridges.
The warning acknowledged that hackers were targeting vulnerabilities in unpatched or internet-linked refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.
Gaining control of these systems would enable hackers to adjust temperatures to dangerous extremes or run unauthorised defrost cycles, leading to the spoilage of inventory or even fire hazards.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT) warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.”

The U.S. FBI-issued factsheet recommended that organisations with cold storage facilities de-link control system devices from the internet, enhance password security, apply patches to keep systems updated, and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates.

The notice came shortly after cyber attacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarket franchises, where some fridge temperatures were raised as high as 50 degrees Celsius in October.
Food and produce had to be thrown out at a mass scale, along with large quantities of melted ice.
The perpetrators behind the attacks have not yet been identified or apprehended.

“Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors. We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” said FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman.

articles.title: Multiple Elector Photo Identity Cards generated for same person during SIR, admits Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Report highlights instances of people holding multiple voter IDs within Mahadevapura, as well as cases where the same Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number appeared in the final electoral rolls of two different Assembly constituencies.

After The Hindu reported that at least 803 voter IDs were linked to 397 people in Mahadevapura Assembly Constituency even after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which was intended to weed out duplicate entries, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, admitted that the discrepancies flagged in the report were due to “procedural circumstances during data processing”.

The report highlighted instances of people holding multiple voter IDs within Mahadevapura, as well as cases where the same Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number appeared in the final electoral rolls of two different Assembly constituencies.

In response, the CEO’s office said that during the SIR, some applicants had submitted multiple Form 6 applications (seeking inclusion) through the Citizen Service Portal. As these applications were “processed independently”, multiple EPIC numbers were inadvertently generated for the same individual.

However, the SIR was intended to identify and eliminate precisely such discrepancies through a comprehensive revision of the electoral rolls to get a “clean roll”. The phased revision process was meant to flag repeat applications, but the system processed them “independently”, allowing multiple voter IDs to slip into the final rolls.

Clarifying how identical EPIC numbers appeared in the final rolls of two constituencies, the CEO’s office said that in some cases, Form 8 applications seeking migration to another constituency had been approved and the electors’ names incorporated into the rolls of their new constituencies. However, the corresponding Form 7 applications seeking deletion of their names from the previous constituencies remained pending.
This was because electoral roll operations had been frozen in accordance with statutory provisions ahead of the final publication of the rolls, the CEO’s office said.
The Hindu had highlighted seven such cases, involving 14 entries where the same EPIC ID number was issued in two different constituencies.

The CEO’s office said that both instances of individuals having multiple EPIC numbers and identical EPIC numbers appearing across two constituencies were a result of “application-processing workflows”.

It added that the cases had been referred to the respective District Election Officers, Additional District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers for rigorous verification and necessary remedial action in accordance with the law.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets 424 additional PG medical seats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Total number of seats rises to 4,196 for 2026-27; 162 of the new seats allotted to government colleges; V-C thanks Naidu and Health Minister for their support

A total of 424 additional postgraduate medical seats have been sanctioned in government and private medical colleges in Andhra Pradesh for the 2026-27 academic year, taking the total number of PG medical seats in the State to 4,196.

According to a release issued by the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare on Saturday, 162 of the additional seats have been allotted to government medical colleges and the remaining to private institutions.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has approved the additional seats, which will be included in the second phase of counselling scheduled for the third week of November. The first phase of counselling for PG medical admissions is under way.
The number of PG medical seats in government medical colleges has increased from 1,915 to 2,077, while the strength in private medical colleges has risen from 1,857 to 2,119.

Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (Dr. NTRUHS) Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar thanked Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav for their support in expanding postgraduate medical education in the State.
He said the expansion would create more opportunities for medical graduates aspiring to pursue postgraduate courses in various specialities.

Among government institutions, Government Medical College, Vizianagaram, has recorded the highest increase, with 28 additional seats, followed by Government Medical College, Paderu, with 24. The other government medical colleges have been allotted fewer than 20 additional seats each.
Among private institutions, Konaseema Institute of Medical Sciences has secured the highest increase, with 59 additional seats, followed by Santhiram Medical College, Nandyal, with 55.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results LIVE: TDP leads in multiple Zilla, Mandal Parishads
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and other top officials are monitoring the counting

Election officials counting votes polled in the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections at a counting centre in Vijayawada today. Officials are seen sorting and verifying ballot papers at designated tables as candidates’ agents and other personnel observe the counting process. The counting was conducted under the supervision of election authorities.

A Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate, who won the MPTC election, celebrates her victory along with party supporters by raising victory signs in Vijayawada today. The results of the MPTC and ZPTC elections across Andhra Pradesh saw candidates of the ruling NDA alliance, comprising the TDP, Jana Sena and BJP, secure victories in several constituencies, prompting celebrations among the winners and their supporters.

Former Minister and YSRCP leader R.K. Roja broke down emotionally after her party’s MPTC candidate from Ilattur in Vijayapuram mandal lost to the TDP nominee by a slender margin of three votes today. The result came after the TDP sought a recount, reportedly following an initial lead for the YSRCP candidate. The narrow defeat triggered tension among YSRCP supporters, with the party questioning the circumstances surrounding the recount. -K. Umashankar
TDP has been declared as a winner in 4 Mandal Parishads in Guntur.

Bapatla District Collector Dr. Vinod Kumar V. (IAS) inspected the counting of votes for ZPTC and MPTC elections in Repalle Revenue Division. The elections were held on November 5 as part of the second ordinary elections to local bodies in the district.
The Collector visited the counting centre set up at the Government Polytechnic College in Repalle town, where votes polled in various mandals under the revenue division were being counted.

He instructed officials to ensure error-free counting by strictly following election rules and guidelines. He stressed the need to maintain utmost care, transparency and accuracy throughout the counting process.
The Telugu Desam Party has won 10 MPTCs and is leading in 60 MPTCs in Guntur district. The party is also leading in 6 ZPTCs.
A media person collapsed after suffering a heart attack while covering election updates at the Narsipatnam counting centre in Anakapalli district.
The journalist was identified as Chintakayala Giri, a representative for Andhra Jyothy from Nathavaram mandal.

articles.title: Bengaluru Metro conducts trial run of Blue Line train at Byappanahalli depot
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line.

The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track. BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly. An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali.
Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line.

The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport. The K.R. Puram–airport stretch is 38.44-km long, while the K.R. Puram–Central Silk Board section covers 19.75 km.

articles.title: Mathematics key to AI’s advancement, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mathematics forms the backbone of modern artificial intelligence (AI), with advanced AI capabilities, predictive power and logical reasoning deeply rooted in mathematical equations, frameworks and data algorithms, said Reheena Nasrin of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Addressing the valedictory session of a three-day international conference on “Computation Science and Intelligent Engineering”, organised by the Department of Mathematics in Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed-to-be-University), she emphasised that strong mathematical foundations would remain essential for the future advancement of digital intelligence.

The final-day technical sessions featured lectures by eminent experts. G. Sobhalatha of Sri Krishnadevaraya University, Anantapur, spoke on ‘Lexicographic Product Graph’, while Bukke Kiran Naik, a scientist from the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Rourkela, delivered a lecture on ‘Intelligent Thermodynamics’, focusing on data-driven systems optimisation and energy-water nexus solutions.

Conference convener Charan announced that more than 200 research papers had been presented by academicians and researchers from reputed universities across India, reflecting the conference’s contribution to academic research and knowledge exchange. Certificates of participation and excellence were distributed to the paper presenters by the dignitaries.
The valedictory session was attended by Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao, Pro-Vice-Chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad, dean D. Venkata Rao and registrar M. Ravichand.

Head of the Mathematics Department Ch. Baby Rani, senior faculty members K. Hemalatha, J. Siva Ram Prasad and M.V.D.N.S. Madhavi, other faculty members, department heads, research scholars and students also participated in the programme.
